Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The Directorate of Education cannot interfere in the day-to-day administration of an unaided minority school.
Reason (R): Article 30(1) of the Constitution provides minorities the absolute right to establish and administer educational institutions without any regulatory checks on academic standards.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Assertion A is treated as true in the source key, while Reason R is false. Article 30(1) protects the right of religious and linguistic minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice, but that right is not absolute immunity from all regulation. The trap is the absolute phrase 'without any regulatory checks', which overstates the scope of the constitutional right.

The core principle is that school discipline must respect a child's dignity and safety; physical punishment and mental harassment are not legitimate disciplinary tools.
